title: Terminating and Recurring Decimals
subject: Mathematics
objective: 1/4 = 0.25 stops, but 1/3 = 0.333… never does. The remainders of long division decide: a remainder of 0 stops it, a returning remainder makes it repeat.

fill.q: If the remainder becomes 0, the decimal ____.
In lowest form, a denominator with only factors 2 and ____ gives a terminating decimal.
1/7 has a repeating block of ____ digits.

tf.explain: 6 has the factor 3, so it recurs.

tf.q: Every rational number is terminating or recurring.
tf.explain: Remainders must end at 0 or repeat.

ar.explain: R is the test that guarantees termination.
A is false (factor 3 makes it recur); R is true.

mcq.q: 1/7 = 0.142857 repeating; the repeating block length is:
Why must long division repeat if it never ends?
options: remainders are less than the divisor, so one returns

num.q: Without long division, decide whether 17/125 and 11/24 terminate. Then write 17/125 as a decimal.

short.q: How can you tell, without dividing, whether 13/40 terminates?
short.solution: Lowest form 13/40; 40 = 2³ × 5 has only 2s and 5s, so it terminates (0.325).

short.q: Write the decimal for 1/7 and explain why it repeats.
short.solution: 0.142857142857… The remainders 1,3,2,6,4,5 cycle back, so the digits repeat with period 6.

match.explain: The remainders decide the type of decimal.
